Question
========
In a boxplot, the median line sits much closer to $Q_1$ than to $Q_3$, and the upper whisker is noticeably longer than
the lower whisker. What does this suggest about the underlying distribution?

Answerlist
----------
* The distribution is roughly symmetric.
* The distribution is right-skewed (positively skewed), with a longer tail toward higher values.
* The distribution is left-skewed (negatively skewed), with a longer tail toward lower values.
* The distribution has no variability.

Solution
========

Answerlist
----------
* Wrong: a symmetric distribution would have the median roughly centered in the box, with whiskers of similar length.
* Correct: a median pulled toward $Q_1$ combined with a longer upper whisker is the signature of a right-skewed distribution.
* Wrong: this pattern would instead show the median pulled toward $Q_3$ with a longer lower whisker.
* Wrong: a distribution with no variability would show a box collapsed to a single line, not this pattern.
